rationale: C08 plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template. Written only days earlier, it contains multiple distinctive formulations that reappear in the child: Congress's repeated cuts to flood-control budget requests, the House's nearly 20 percent cut, the constraint on spending during the emergency, characterization of further cuts as false economy, the need for long-term comprehensive river planning, and the linked purposes of flood prevention, power production, navigation, irrigation, and other benefits. The child expands this same argument into a detailed appropriations request. C01 and C07 share the congressional-appropriations structure of urging the Senate to reverse House cuts, but their overlap is less distinctive and material than C08's flood-control language and reasoning.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The House cut my budget requests for this important work by nearly 20 per cent
shared_material.parent_excerpt: just a few weeks ago the House of Representatives cut this year's budget requests by nearly 20 percent
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim statement of the same House reduction to flood-control appropriations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: We can spend little enough on this kind of work in emergency times like the present. For the last several years I have not been able to include in the budget as much money for flood control and river and harbor work as I would have liked
shared_material.parent_excerpt: We can spend little enough on flood control in emergency times like these, and I have had to hold my budget requests for flood control far below what I would have liked to recommend.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared phrasing and identical argumentative function: the original requests were already constrained by emergency conditions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I believe this cut was false economy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I believe that cuts even below the budget requests would be the most dangerous kind of false economy.
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize reductions below the already limited flood-control budget as false economy.

shared_material.child_excerpt: steady, well planned progress in this field—as contrasted with hasty, stop-and-go action, prompted by temporary incidents. The task of controlling our great rivers ... is a long-range task, which must be tackled with long-range plans.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the need for long-term, comprehensive planning in this field. You have worked steadily, year in and year out, for sensible, effective control and use of our great rivers
shared_material.explanation: The child develops C08's long-term-planning theme and contrast between steady policy and episodic reaction to floods.

shared_material.child_excerpt: use and control our water resources to prevent floods, provide navigation, produce power, and bring other benefits
shared_material.parent_excerpt: control and use of our great rivers to prevent floods, to produce power, to irrigate lands, and to yield the other benefits that can come from wise river basin development
shared_material.explanation: Closely parallel enumeration of the multiple purposes served by river-development projects.
